## 2. Verified Statutory Anchors

### 2.1 Form XXV — Annual Return to the Karnataka Welfare Board

**Verified anchor.** The BOCW Central Rules prescribe **Form XXV** as the annual return to be filed with the state Welfare Board. Filing is due **by 15 February** for the preceding calendar year.

- **Filing authority:** Karnataka Building & Other Construction Workers' Welfare Board
- **Filing due:** 15 February each year (calendar year basis)
- **Next filing:** 15 February 2027 (for calendar year 2026); calendar year 2025 return was due 15 February 2026 — verify currency
- **Cite:** BOCW Central Rules; KB-REG-IN-STATEFORMS row `bocw | All | annual-return | Form XXV`

### 2.2 Welfare Cess — 1% of Cost of Construction

**Verified anchor.** The Building & Other Construction Workers' Welfare Cess Act 1996 imposes a cess of **1% of the cost of construction** on every establishment employing ten or more building workers. The cess is remitted to the Karnataka Welfare Board. The principal employer holds primary liability; construction costs attributable to both own-force and contracted-out works are included in the assessment base.

- **Cite:** Building & Other Construction Workers' Welfare Cess Act 1996

## 4. Compliance Gap-List

### Gap 1 — Establishment Registration (BOCW Act s.7)

**Requirement:** Every establishment employing ten or more building workers must be registered with the Karnataka Welfare Board.

**Position:** At ~250 workers the registration trigger (≥10) is unambiguously met. Whether valid registration is in place has not been confirmed.

**Risk:** Operating without registration is a criminal offence under s.7 BOCW Act; workers are also disqualified from Board benefits until the establishment is registered.

**Action:** The principal employer to produce the valid Karnataka Welfare Board BOCW Registration Certificate within **14 days (by 19 July 2026)**. If registration has not yet been obtained, submit the application to the Karnataka Welfare Board immediately — do not defer.

---

### Gap 2 — Welfare Cess Payment Evidence (BOCW Cess Act 1996)

**Requirement:** 1% cess on the cost of construction must be assessed, paid, and evidenced. The principal employer bears primary liability; labour contractor portions are aggregated into the same assessment base.

**Position:** No cess payment receipts or assessment correspondence have been sighted in the engagement facts.

**Risk:** Cess arrears attract interest and penalty. Outstanding cess is frequently a pre-condition for Board co-operation on worker registrations and welfare claims.

**Action:** The principal employer (financial/contracts role) to produce cess assessment letters and payment receipts for the current project — covering both own-force and contracted-out works — within **30 days (by 4 August 2026)**. If assessment is outstanding, engage the competent authority immediately to regularise.

---

### Gap 3 — Form XXV Annual Return Currency (BOCW Central Rules)

**Requirement:** Form XXV filed with the Karnataka Welfare Board by 15 February each year.

**Position:** Calendar year 2025 return was due 15 February 2026; filing currency has not been confirmed. The next filing (calendar year 2026) falls due 15 February 2027.

**Risk:** Late or non-filing is a statutory default; the Board may pursue enforcement and the gap will be adverse in any labour inspection.

**Action:**
- (a) The principal employer (compliance role) to confirm that the Form XXV for calendar year 2025 was filed on time and to produce the Board's acknowledgement within **14 days (by 19 July 2026)**.
- (b) Diarise the Form XXV filing for calendar year 2026 now: due date **15 February 2027**.

### Gap 4 — Safety Officer Appointment and Safety Committee Constitution

**Requirement:** Appointment of a qualified Safety Officer (role) and constitution of a Safety Committee above the Karnataka-notified headcount threshold.

**[GAP] — Karnataka threshold not verified: see §3 above.**

**Position:** With ~250 workers, the threshold is plausibly met. No Safety Officer appointment has been confirmed in the engagement facts.

**Risk:** If the threshold is met and no Safety Officer is in post, the establishment is in default under the BOCW Central Rules. In the event of a fatality or serious accident, absence of a Safety Officer will be an aggravating factor in any prosecution.

**Action:**
- (a) The principal employer (site management role) to verify the current Karnataka-notified Safety Officer headcount threshold with the Karnataka Labour Department / Board within **14 days (by 19 July 2026)**.
- (b) If the threshold is met (or pending confirmation), appoint a qualified Safety Officer (role) and constitute the Safety Committee within **30 days of confirming the threshold** — at the latest by **4 August 2026** if confirmation is obtained promptly.
- (c) Document the appointment in writing; retain the appointment letter and committee constitution record on site.

### Gap 5 — Worker Beneficiary Registration (BOCW Act s.12)

**Requirement:** Each building worker aged 18–60 who has worked for ≥90 days in a year is entitled to be registered as a beneficiary with the Karnataka Welfare Board. Both the principal employer and contractors have a duty to facilitate registration.

**Position:** Beneficiary registration status of the ~250 workers has not been confirmed in the engagement facts.

**Risk:** Unregistered workers cannot access Board benefits (group insurance, pension contributions, medical assistance, education support). The employer faces enforcement for non-facilitation.

**Action:** The principal employer (co-ordination role) and each of the two labour contractors (for their own workers) to conduct a beneficiary registration audit — identify all workers who meet the 90-day threshold and remain unregistered — and complete bulk registration with the Karnataka Welfare Board within **60 days (by 3 September 2026)**.

---

### Gap 6 — Welfare Amenities (BOCW Act Chapter IV)

**Requirement:** The BOCW Act mandates welfare amenities above specified worker thresholds: canteen, rest rooms/shelters, first-aid facilities, potable water, and a crèche where female workers with young children are present.

**Position:** At ~250 workers, multiple amenity thresholds are likely met. Adequacy has not been audited against the engagement facts.

**Risk:** Non-provision is a direct statutory default; inadequate amenities will be an adverse finding on any Board or labour inspection, and compound the risk profile in the event of injury.

**Action:** The principal employer (welfare/site role) to commission a **welfare amenities walkdown** against BOCW Act Chapter IV requirements within **30 days (by 4 August 2026)**; produce a written record of compliance/gaps; remediate all gaps within **60 days (by 3 September 2026)**.

---

### Gap 7 — Statutory Registers (BOCW Act / Central Rules)

**Requirement:** Prescribed registers must be maintained on site: register of workers, wages register, attendance register, overtime register, and others as notified under the Central Rules.

**Position:** Register currency and completeness have not been confirmed.

**Risk:** Incomplete or missing registers are a statutory default and a reliable trigger for adverse inspection outcomes.

**Action:** The principal employer and each of the two labour contractors to produce and review their statutory registers for completeness and currency within **14 days (by 19 July 2026)**; remediate any gaps immediately. The principal employer to retain a site-level verification record.

---

### Gap 8 — Contractor Compliance Verification

**Requirement:** The principal employer has a duty to ensure that labour contractors on site are themselves BOCW-compliant: registered, cess-paid, and with workers registered with the Board.

**Position:** No contractor compliance certificates have been sighted for either of the two labour contractors.

**Risk:** Where a contractor defaults, the principal employer may face derivative liability for cess arrears, worker registrations, and welfare obligations. This is the standard enforcement posture of state Welfare Boards.

**Action:** The principal employer (contracts/procurement role) to obtain from each of the two labour contractors within **30 days (by 4 August 2026)**: (a) BOCW registration certificate; (b) cess payment evidence; (c) worker beneficiary registration status; (d) copies of current statutory registers. Withhold work-order extensions pending receipt.

### Gap 9 — Accident Notification Procedure (BOCW Act s.39)

**Requirement:** Fatal and serious accidents on site must be notified to the prescribed authority within the state-prescribed time and on the state-prescribed form.

**[GAP] — Karnataka-specific accident notification form and mandatory reporting timeframe NOT verified in the knowledge base.**

**Risk:** Failure to notify a reportable accident within the required period is a criminal offence under s.39 BOCW Act and may prejudice workers' compensation and Board benefit claims.

**Action:** The Safety Officer (role) / principal employer to confirm with the Karnataka Labour Department: (a) the prescribed form for fatal/serious accident notification under the Karnataka BOCW Rules; (b) the mandatory notification timeframe. Document the confirmed procedure, brief the site emergency co-ordinator, and post the relevant authority contact on the site notice board — within **14 days (by 19 July 2026)**.

## 6. OSH Code 2020 — Transition Note

The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (Act 37 of 2020) consolidates the BOCW Act 1996 — together with twelve other central labour laws — into a single registration and single consolidated annual return **in principle**. For this site today, the position is:

- **Karnataka has not notified its OSH Rules** under the Code as of 5 July 2026. The Code's savings clause keeps legacy BOCW filings valid until commencement is notified in each state.
- **Legacy-first applies:** the BOCW registration, Form XXV annual return, and 1% cess obligations set out in this memo are the **operative, legally defensible obligations** for this Karnataka site now.
- When Karnataka notifies its OSH Rules, the consolidated registration and single consolidated return will in principle supersede the legacy filings — but the forms and portal may not be live immediately. Verify with the Karnataka Labour Department and Karnataka Welfare Board before transitioning away from legacy filings.

> **Freshness note:** OSH Code commencement is state-by-state and actively in flux. This transition note should be refreshed within **90 days (by 3 October 2026)**, or sooner if Karnataka publishes a gazette notification on OSH Rules commencement.

*(Cite: KB-REG-IN-OSH-CODE; KB-REG-IN-BOCW §OSH-Code transition note)*
